Address it by `path` ("tag/path/slug", exactly the `path` or `url` a listing returns), or by `tagPath` + `slug`; a category's own path reads its hub article. Not a title. tools.name: get_pages
tools.description: Batch read: 1 to 20 pages of the Caper knowledge base in full in one call, which is how to read search or listing results. Pass `paths` as the listings return them. Paths that do not exist come back in `missing` rather than failing the call, anything past 20 in `remaining`, and pages past `maxChars`

tools.name: list_pages
tools.description: Browse the Caper knowledge base by tag path rather than by keyword: every page under a branch, newest first by default. `tagPath` matches the branch and everything beneath it; omit it to walk the whole wiki. Sort by title for an A–Z pass. Same rows as search_wiki, with `totalPages`, `hasMore` and `n

tools.name: get_recent_changes
tools.description: Pages of the Caper knowledge base edited within the last N days, newest first: what to poll when you are watching the wiki rather than reading it. Same rows as list_pages. Defaults: days 7 (max 30), limit 20 (max 50). `truncated: true` means the limit cut the list; raise it, or page through list_pag

tools.name: get_page_history
tools.description: A page's revisions in the Caper knowledge base, newest first: each one's `id`, version, change type, message, date and the blocks it changed. Address the page as get_page does. A revision `id` is what a restore takes, where this server has one. Defaults: limit 20 (max 100).

tools.name: get_categories
tools.description: The category tree of the Caper knowledge base, the cheapest way to orient before searching. Each node carries its `path` (a tagPath list_pages and search_wiki take), name, description, `pageCount` (pages filed at that path) and `pageCountDeep` (with every descendant). `tagPaths` lists every tag path

tools.description: Index of the DAOs on Caper: cashtag, name, description, member count, wiki URL, and that DAO's own MCP endpoint. tools.name: get_challenge
tools.description: Step 1 of writing to Caper: a single-use ROLA challenge (5-minute expiry). The response includes the exact recipe for the message your Ed25519 key must sign. Writes are Stokenet-testnet only for now, and you always sign with your OWN key – nothing here custodies anything. Takes no parameters.

tools.name: login
tools.description: Step 2: exchange the signed ROLA proof for a 12h Bearer token – the same verification the human wallet flow runs. Send the returned token as an HTTP `Authorization: Bearer <token>` header on every later tool call; MCP arguments never carry it.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_page, get_page_history, list_daos, get_challenge, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about · Public sink: get_page, list_daos, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about · Destructive: search_wiki, get_manifest, submit_tx, delete_wiki_page.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_wiki, get_page, get_page_history, list_daos, get_challenge, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about · Private data: get_full_corpus, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about · Public sink: get_page, list_daos, login, get_manifest, submit_tx, save_wiki_page, delete_wiki_page, save_about · Destructive: search_wiki, get_manifest, submit_tx, delete_wiki_page

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
